questions.q_en: According to Article 265 of the Indian Constitution, what is the key principle regarding the collection of taxes in India?
options_en: No tax shall be levied or collected without prior approval from the judiciary.
No tax shall be levied or collected except by authority of law.
Taxes must be levied by Parliament, but collection is managed by states.
The Finance Ministry can levy taxes with retrospective effect.
questions.solution_en:
• Article 265 of the Constitution establishes that taxation can only be done by legal authority. This principle ensures that taxes cannot be arbitrarily imposed by any entity without due legislation.

• Judiciary does not approve tax laws but can review their constitutionality.

• Both Parliament and state legislatures levy taxes based on their respective jurisdictions.

• Retrospective taxation can occur, but it must be done through legislative action, not solely by the Finance Ministry.

Further Insight:

• Taxation in India is structured across a three-tier federal system, where the Centre, State, and Local Governments hold the authority to levy and collect taxes.

• This power is explicitly provided by the Constitution of India.

• Part XII of Constitution of India - Finance, Property, Contracts and Suits

○ Article 265 - No tax shall be levied or collected except by authority of law.

○ Article 266 - Consolidated Funds and public accounts of India and of the States.

○ Article 267 - Contingency Fund.

• Distribution of Revenues between the Union and the States

○ Article 268 - Duties levied by the Union but collected and appropriated by the States.

○ Article 269 - Taxes levied and collected by the Union but assigned to the States.

○ Article 269A - Levy and collection of goods and services tax in course of inter-State trade or commerce.

○ Article 270 - Taxes levied and distributed between the Union and the States.
questions.solution_hi:
• संविधान का अनुच्छेद 265 स्थापित करता है कि कराधान केवल कानूनी प्राधिकार द्वारा ही किया जा सकता है। यह सिद्धांत सुनिश्चित करता है कि उचित विधान के बिना कोई भी संस्था मनमाने ढंग से कर नहीं लगा सकती।

• न्यायपालिका कर कानूनों को स्वीकृत नहीं करती परंतु उनकी संवैधानिकता की समीक्षा कर सकती है।

questions.q_en: Which of the following is considered a progressive tax in India, primarily aimed at reducing income inequality?
questions.solution_en:
• Income tax is progressive in nature, meaning higher income levels attract higher tax rates.

○ This is designed to distribute the tax burden more equitably, reducing income inequality.

• GST is a proportional tax

• Customs Duty is levied on imports and exports. It is not based on income levels.

• Excise Duty is imposed on goods produced within the country and does not have a progressive nature.

Further Insight:

• Progressive tax: It is a type of taxation system in which the government takes a larger percentage of income as tax from high-income groups than from low-income groups. E,g Direct taxes such as Income tax.

• Proportional tax: It is a type of taxation system in which the government takes the same percentage of income as tax from all income groups. E.g Indirect taxes such as GST.

• Regressive tax: It is a type of taxation system in which the government takes a larger percentage of income as tax from low-income groups than from high-income groups. E.g Indirect taxes whose burden mainly falls on low income group.
questions.solution_hi:
• आयकर प्रकृति में प्रगतिशील है, अर्थात उच्च आय स्तर पर अधिक कर दरें लगती हैं।

○ इसे कर बोझ को अधिक न्यायसंगत रूप से वितरित करने, आय असमानता घटाने हेतु डिज़ाइन किया गया है।

• GST एक आनुपातिक कर है।

• सीमा शुल्क आयात व निर्यात पर लगाया जाता है।

questions.q_en: Why are indirect taxes called regressive?
options_en: They are charged at higher rates than direct tax
They are charged at the same rate for all income groups.
None of the above are correct
questions.solution_en:
• Low and high income earners pay the same amount under a regressive tax, which is a kind of tax imposed regardless of income.

○ Low-income taxpayers are more negatively impacted than high-income earners.

• Regardless of their financial situation, everyone who purchases goods must pay indirect taxes and they are charged at the same rate for all income groups..

○ It is a regressive tax since the poor will pay a higher percentage of their income in taxes than the rich people.

• Indirect taxes called regressive as

Further Insight:

• Indirect taxes are levied on goods and services, where the tax burden is passed on to the final consumer. These are typically regressive as they apply uniformly regardless of income.

• Examples:

○ Goods and Services Tax (GST): A comprehensive tax covering all goods and services.

○ Customs Duty: Levied on imports and exports.

○ Excise Duty: Levied on the production of goods within the country.

• The Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC) administers indirect taxes.
questions.solution_hi:
• निम्न व उच्च आय अर्जक प्रतिगामी कर के तहत समान राशि भुगतान करते हैं, जो एक ऐसा कर है जो आय की परवाह किए बिना लगाया जाता है।

○ निम्न आय वाले करदाता उच्च आय अर्जकों की तुलना में अधिक नकारात्मक रूप से प्रभावित होते हैं।

questions.q_en: With enactment of which act the modern taxation system in India begin to evolve, ultimately leading to the enactment of the Income Tax Act of 1961?
questions.solution_en:
• The modern taxation system began evolving under British rule, with the introduction of the first Income Tax Act in 1860, which laid the foundation for today's tax system culminating in the Income Tax Act of 1961.

Further Insight:

• The modern taxation system began in 1860 under James Wilson, who introduced the Income Tax Act to cover the fiscal deficits following the Revolt of 1857.

• Later, the Income Tax Act of 1922 formed the base for today's taxation system which is largely governed by the Income Tax Act of 1961(It was recommended by the Direct Taxes Enquiry Committee).
questions.solution_hi:
• आधुनिक कराधान प्रणाली ब्रिटिश शासन के तहत विकसित होना शुरू हुई, 1860 में पहला आयकर अधिनियम पेश किए जाने के साथ, जिसने आज की कर प्रणाली की नींव रखी जो 1961 के आयकर अधिनियम में समाप्त हुई।

• आधुनिक कराधान प्रणाली 1860 में जेम्स विल्सन के अधीन शुरू हुई।

questions.q_en: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between CGST, SGST, and IGST under the Goods and Services Tax regime?
options_en: CGST and SGST apply on inter-state transactions, while IGST applies on intra-state transactions.
CGST is collected by the state government, SGST by the central government, and IGST is shared equally.
CGST and SGST apply on intra-state transactions, while IGST applies on inter-state transactions.
Only IGST applies on both inter-state and intra-state transactions.
questions.solution_en:
• CGST (Central Goods and Services Tax) and SGST (State Goods and Services Tax) apply to transactions within a state, while IGST (Integrated Goods and Services Tax) applies to transactions between states or on imports.

• CGST and SGST do not apply to inter-state transactions. (Inter means with two different bodies, Intra means within the same body.)

• CGST is collected by the central government, and SGST is collected by state governments; IGST is collected by the central government but distributed as per rules.

• IGST only applies to inter-state transactions, not intra-state ones.

Further Insight:

• Goods and Services Tax (GST)

○ Passed and added in constitution after 101st Constitutional amendment Bill 2016

○ Implemented on July 1, 2017, GST is a multi-stage, destination-based tax.

○ It is aimed at eliminating the cascading effect of previous taxes.

○ GST integrates most indirect taxes into a single tax system.

○ It is divided into CGST, SGST, and IGST (for inter-state transactions).

• GST Council:

○ Decision-making body chaired by the Finance Minister of India mentioned in Article 279A.

○ It includes the Union and State Finance Ministers.

○ The Union has 1/3rd voting power while the state has 2/3rd voting power.

■ To pass any bill it must be passed by 3/4th vote

○ The council oversees changes in GST rates, exemptions, and procedural regulations

• Exemptions under GST

○ Custom duty will be still collected along with the levy of IGST on imported goods.

○ Petroleum and tobacco products are currently exempted.

○ Excise duty on liquor, stamp duty and electricity taxes are also exempted.
questions.solution_hi:
• CGST (केंद्रीय वस्तु एवं सेवा कर) व SGST (राज्य वस्तु एवं सेवा कर) किसी राज्य के भीतर लेनदेन पर लागू होते हैं, जबकि IGST (एकीकृत वस्तु एवं सेवा कर) राज्यों के बीच लेनदेन या आयात पर लागू होता है।

• CGST व SGST अंतर-राज्यीय लेनदेन पर लागू नहीं होते।

questions.q_en: As per Section 115BBH of the Income Tax Act, how is the income from cryptocurrency taxed in India?
options_en: Tax-free under the Digital Economy Promotion Act
Flat 30% tax rate, without any deductions
10% tax on long-term gains, 20% on short-term gains
Progressive tax based on income slabs
questions.solution_en:
• Cryptocurrency income is taxed at a flat 30% rate as per Section 115BBH of the Income Tax Act.

• No deduction, except the cost of acquisition, are allowed.

• Cryptocurrency is taxed at a flat rate of 30%, not differentiated by short or long-term gains.

Further Insight:

• Taxation on Virtual Digital Assets (Cryptocurrency)

• Introduced: 2022-23 Budget.

• Tax Rate: 30% on income from the transfer of virtual digital assets.

• No Deductions: Except for the cost of acquisition.

• 1% TDS: On transactions over a specific threshold.

• Impact:

• Aims to regulate the growing cryptocurrency market.

• Encourages transparency in digital asset transactions.
questions.solution_hi:
• आयकर अधिनियम की धारा 115BBH के अनुसार क्रिप्टोकरेंसी आय पर सपाट 30% दर से कर लगाया जाता है।

• अधिग्रहण लागत को छोड़कर कोई कटौती अनुमति नहीं है।

• क्रिप्टोकरेंसी पर सपाट 30% दर से कर लगता है, अल्पकालिक या दीर्घकालिक लाभ के अनुसार अलग नहीं।

questions.q_en: Which of the following is an example of a tax levied specifically by state governments and not the central government?
questions.solution_en:
• Entertainment Tax is levied by state governments on activities such as movie screenings, amusement parks, and events.

• Customs Duty, Income Tax and Corporation Tax are levied by the central government.

Further Insight:

• State Taxes:

○ Levied by State Governments:

○ Types of State tax:

○ State Goods and Services Tax (SGST): State portion of GST for intra-state sales.

○ Stamp Duty: On property transactions and official documents.

○ Entertainment Tax: On events like movies and concerts (now mostly subsumed under GST).

• Exemptions under GST

○ Custom duty is still collected along with the levy of IGST on imported goods.

○ Petroleum and tobacco products are exempted.

○ Excise duty on liquor, stamp duty and electricity taxes are exempted.
questions.solution_hi:
• मनोरंजन कर राज्य सरकारों द्वारा फिल्म प्रदर्शन, मनोरंजन पार्क व आयोजनों जैसी गतिविधियों पर लगाया जाता है।

• सीमा शुल्क, आयकर व कॉर्पोरेशन कर केंद्र सरकार द्वारा लगाए जाते हैं।

• राज्य कर: राज्य सरकारों द्वारा लगाए जाते हैं।

questions.q_en: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution is the distribution of tax revenues between the Union and the States outlined?
questions.solution_en:
• Article 270 of the Constitution details the sharing of tax revenues between the Union and the States.

○ It addresses taxes that are levied by the Union but shared with the States based on the recommendations of the Finance Commission.

• Article 268 deals with duties levied by the Union but collected and appropriated by the States.

• Article 280 relates to the Finance Commission, which recommends the distribution of revenues.

• Article 246 defines the legislative powers between the Union and State governments.

Further Insight:

Part XII of Constitution of India - Finance, Property, Contracts and Suits

○ Article 265 - No tax shall be levied or collected except by authority of law.

○ Article 266 - Consolidated Funds and public accounts of India and of the States.

○ Article 267 - Contingency Fund.

• Distribution of Revenues between the Union and the States

○ Article 268 - Duties levied by the Union but collected and appropriated by the States.

○ Article 269 - Taxes levied and collected by the Union but assigned to the States.

○ Article 269A - Levy and collection of goods and services tax in course of inter-State trade or commerce.

○ Article 270 - Taxes levied and distributed between the Union and the States.

○ Article 275 - Grants from the Union to certain States.

○ Article 279A - Goods and Services Tax Council.

○ Article 280 - Finance Commission.

○ Article 281 - Recommendations of the Finance Commission.
questions.solution_hi:
• संविधान का अनुच्छेद 270 केंद्र व राज्यों के बीच कर राजस्व साझाकरण का विवरण देता है।

○ यह उन करों को संबोधित करता है जो केंद्र द्वारा लगाए जाते हैं परंतु वित्त आयोग की सिफारिशों के आधार पर राज्यों के साथ साझा किए जाते हैं।

• अनुच्छेद 268 केंद्र द्वारा लगाए गए परंतु राज्यों द्वारा एकत्रित शुल्कों से संबंधित है।

questions.q_en: Which of the following taxes falls under the category of direct taxes in India?
questions.solution_en:
• Securities Transaction Tax (STT) is a direct tax that is levied on the purchase or sale of securities listed on Indian stock exchanges. It is directly borne by the individual or entity engaged in the transaction.

• VAT is an indirect tax, collected from consumers but remitted by businesses to the government.

• Service Tax was an indirect tax, now subsumed under GST.

• Excise Duty is also an indirect tax, imposed on the manufacture of goods.

Further Insight:

• Direct Taxes

○ Direct taxes are levied directly on the income or wealth of individuals or organizations, and the burden cannot be shifted.

○ These taxes are mostly progressive, meaning the tax rate increases with higher income.

○ Examples:

■ Income Tax: Levied on the income of individuals and businesses.

■ Corporate Tax: Applied to the profits of companies.

■ Capital Gains Tax: Tax on the sale of capital assets.

■ Securities Transaction Tax (STT): Imposed on transactions in securities markets.
questions.solution_hi:
• प्रतिभूति लेनदेन कर (STT) एक प्रत्यक्ष कर है जो भारतीय शेयर बाजारों में सूचीबद्ध प्रतिभूतियों की खरीद या बिक्री पर लगाया जाता है। यह लेनदेन में शामिल व्यक्ति या संस्था द्वारा सीधे वहन किया जाता है।

• VAT एक अप्रत्यक्ष कर है।

questions.q_en: Before the introduction of GST, which of the following was an indirect tax levied at both the Central and State levels in India?
questions.solution_en:
• VAT was a major indirect tax applied by both the central and state governments before GST.

○ It was collected on the sale of goods, with different rates in different states.

• Central Excise Duty was levied on goods manufactured in India and was a central government tax.

• Custom Duty is levied on imports and exports, also by the central government.

• Income Tax is a direct tax.

Further Insight:

• VAT (Value Added Tax)

○ VAT is an indirect tax levied on goods and services at each stage of production, from raw materials to the final product.

○ It is charged on the value additions at different production stages.

○ Value Added Tax was incorporated into the Indian taxation system on 1st April 2005, replacing Sales Tax.

○ The Goods and Services Tax (GST) is a value-added tax that is poised to be implemented in India, which will replace all indirect taxes levied on goods and services by the Indian Central and State governments
questions.solution_hi:
• VAT GST से पहले केंद्र व राज्य दोनों सरकारों द्वारा लागू एक प्रमुख अप्रत्यक्ष कर था।

○ यह वस्तुओं की बिक्री पर एकत्रित किया जाता था, विभिन्न राज्यों में अलग-अलग दरों के साथ।

• केंद्रीय उत्पाद शुल्क भारत में निर्मित वस्तुओं पर लगाया जाता था।

questions.q_en: Which tax introduced during British rule in India was directly levied on landholders and had a profound effect on agriculture?
questions.solution_en:
• Land Revenue was a tax directly levied on landholders during British rule, particularly under the Permanent Settlement of Bengal. It had a significant impact on Indian agriculture and the rural economy.

• Property Tax is a modern concept applied in urban areas.

• Wealth Tax was introduced in independent India but has been abolished.

• Jizya was a tax levied on non-Muslims during the Mughal period and before in Delhi Sultanate, unrelated to land or agriculture.

Further Insight:

• Permanent Settlement (1793)

○ Introduced by Lord Cornwallis

○ It was implemented in Bengal, Bihar, parts of Orissa

○ Key Provisions:

■ Revenue was a fixed annual amount, not subject to revision.

■ Zamindars (landowners) were responsible for paying the fixed revenue.

○ Led to commercialization and exploitation of farmers( zamindars had control over peasants, often leading to economic distress among farmers.)

• Ryotwari System

○ Introduced by Thomas Munro

○ Implemented in Madras, Bombay, parts of Assam, Central India

○ Key Provisions:

■ Revenue was directly assessed on the land and crop yield, with payments made by individual farmers (ryots).

■ Farmers had occupancy rights and were directly accountable to the government.

○ It provided more security to farmers and was adaptable to local conditions, though it faced challenges with land records and revenue assessment.

• Mahalwari System

• Introduced by: Holt Mackenzie

• Implemented in North-Western Provinces (now Uttar Pradesh), Punjab, Central India

• Key Provisions:

○ Revenue was collected from the head of a mahal (village or group of villages) based on land productivity.

○ Land Tenure: Shared responsibility among the community; the revenue was based on collective accountability.

• Impact: Aimed to balance interests but often led to administrative complexities and disputes over land rights.
questions.solution_hi:
• भूमि राजस्व ब्रिटिश शासन के दौरान भूस्वामियों पर सीधे लगाया जाने वाला एक कर था, विशेषकर बंगाल के स्थायी बंदोबस्त के तहत। इसका भारतीय कृषि व ग्रामीण अर्थव्यवस्था पर महत्वपूर्ण प्रभाव पड़ा।

• संपत्ति कर शहरी क्षेत्रों में लागू एक आधुनिक अवधारणा है।

questions.q_en: What is the primary reason why the implementation of GST is considered a destination-based tax?
options_en: Taxes are collected at the origin of goods and services.
The tax is levied where goods and services are produced.
Taxes are collected where goods and services are consumed.
Taxes are shared between both the origin and destination states.
questions.solution_en:
• GST is a destination-based tax, meaning the tax is levied at the place where goods or services are finally consumed, rather than where they are produced. This helps in creating a uniform tax structure across states.

• GST does not operate on an origin-based principle.

• Production does not determine GST application.

• Taxes are not shared between the origin and destination states in this manner.

Further Insight:

• Goods and Services Tax (GST)

○ Introduced: July 1, 2017.

○ Introduced by 101st Constitutional Act,2016

○ Structure: Divided into CGST, SGST, and IGST (for inter-state transactions).

○ Key Features:

■ Destination based Taxation

■ Unified tax structure across the country.

■ Removed cascading tax effects (tax on tax).

■ Replaced indirect taxes like VAT, Excise, and Service Tax.
questions.solution_hi:
• GST एक गंतव्य-आधारित कर है, अर्थात कर उस स्थान पर लगाया जाता है जहाँ वस्तुओं या सेवाओं का अंतिम उपभोग होता है, न कि जहाँ उनका उत्पादन होता है। यह राज्यों में एक समान कर संरचना बनाने में मदद करता है।

• GST मूल-आधारित सिद्धांत पर कार्य नहीं करता।

questions.q_en: Under the Indian tax regime, which of the following applies to the taxation of income earned from cryptocurrency trading?
options_en: Income from cryptocurrency trading is treated as capital gains and taxed accordingly.
A flat tax rate of 30% is applied, without the option for set-off against other income.
Cryptocurrency trading income is exempt from tax if held for more than one year.
It is taxed based on the individual's income slab.
questions.solution_en:
• The Indian government has imposed a flat 30% tax rate on income from cryptocurrency trading, and no deduction or set-off against other income is permitted under Section 115BBH of the Income Tax Act.

• Cryptocurrency income is not treated as capital gains, but taxed separately.

• There is no exemption for cryptocurrency income based on holding period.

• The tax rate is flat at 30%, not based on income slabs.

Further Insight:

• Taxation on Virtual Digital Assets (Cryptocurrency)

• Introduced: 2022-23 Budget.

• Tax Rate: 30% on income from the transfer of virtual digital assets.

• No Deductions: Except for the cost of acquisition.

• 1% TDS: On transactions over a specific threshold.

• Impact:

• Aims to regulate the growing cryptocurrency market.

• Encourages transparency in digital asset transactions.
questions.solution_hi:
• भारत सरकार ने आयकर अधिनियम की धारा 115BBH के तहत क्रिप्टोकरेंसी ट्रेडिंग से आय पर सपाट 30% कर दर लगाई है, व अन्य आय के विरुद्ध कोई कटौती या समायोजन की अनुमति नहीं है।

• क्रिप्टोकरेंसी आय को पूँजीगत लाभ नहीं माना जाता, बल्कि अलग से कर लगाया जाता है।

questions.q_en: Which of the following taxes is exclusively under the purview of state governments as per the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution_en:
• State Excise Duty is levied by state governments on alcohol, narcotics, and other excisable goods produced within a state. It is one of the major revenue sources for state governments.

• Corporation Tax is levied by the central government on corporate profits.

• Capital Gains Tax is also under the central government's domain.

• Securities Transaction Tax (STT) is levied by the central government.

Further Insight:

• Central Taxes:

○ Taxes levied and collected by the Central Government:

■ Income Tax: Tax on individual income.

■ Excise Duty: On production and manufacturing of goods.

■ Customs Duty: Tax on imports and exports.

■ CGST (Central Goods and Services Tax): Component of GST on intra-state transactions.

• State Taxes:

○ Levied by State Governments:

■ State Goods and Services Tax (SGST): State portion of GST for intra-state sales.

■ Stamp Duty: On property transactions and official documents.

■ Entertainment Tax: On events like movies and concerts (now mostly subsumed under GST).
questions.solution_hi:
• राज्य उत्पाद शुल्क राज्य सरकारों द्वारा किसी राज्य में उत्पादित शराब, नशीले पदार्थों व अन्य उत्पाद-योग्य वस्तुओं पर लगाया जाता है। यह राज्य सरकारों हेतु प्रमुख राजस्व स्रोतों में से एक है।

• कॉर्पोरेशन कर केंद्र सरकार द्वारा कॉर्पोरेट लाभ पर लगाया जाता है।

questions.q_en:
Consider the following statements about taxation in India:

a) Income Tax in India was first introduced in the year 1860 by Sir James Wilson.

b) The Constitution of India divides the power to levy taxes between the Union and the States.

c) Finance Commission is constituted under Article 265 of the Constitution of India.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution_en:
• Income tax was first introduced in India by Sir James Wilson in 1860 to meet the revenue demands of the British government.

• The Constitution divides tax powers between the Union and States.

• The Finance Commission is constituted under Article 280, not Article 265. Article 265 states that no tax shall be levied or collected except by the authority of law.

Further Insight:

• The modern taxation system began in 1860 under James Wilson, who introduced the Income Tax Act to cover the fiscal deficits following the Revolt of 1857.

○ Later, the Income Tax Act of 1922 formed the base for today's taxation system which is largely governed by the Income Tax Act of 1961(It was recommended by the Direct Taxes Enquiry Committee).

• Part XII of Constitution of India - Finance, Property, Contracts and Suits

○ Article 265 - No tax shall be levied or collected except by authority of law.

○ Article 266 - Consolidated Funds and public accounts of India and of the States.

○ Article 267 - Contingency Fund.

• Distribution of Revenues between the Union and the States

○ Article 275 - Grants from the Union to certain States.

○ Article 279A - Goods and Services Tax Council.

○ Article 280 - Finance Commission.

○ Article 281 - Recommendations of the Finance Commission.
questions.solution_hi:
• आयकर पहली बार 1860 में सर जेम्स विल्सन द्वारा ब्रिटिश सरकार की राजस्व माँगों को पूरा करने हेतु भारत में पेश किया गया था।

• संविधान केंद्र व राज्यों के बीच कर शक्तियों का विभाजन करता है।

• वित्त आयोग अनुच्छेद 280 के तहत गठित होता है, अनुच्छेद 265 नहीं।

questions.q_en:
Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding direct taxes in India?

a) Direct taxes are levied on individuals or organizations and cannot be shifted to others.

b) Wealth Tax, which was abolished in 2015, was a direct tax.

c) Corporate Tax is an indirect tax on businesses.
questions.solution_en:
• Direct taxes, such as income tax, are paid directly by the taxpayer.

• Wealth Tax was a direct tax until it was abolished in 2015.

• Corporate Tax is a direct tax, not an indirect tax, as it is levied directly on the income or profits of companies.

Further Insight:

• Direct Taxes

○ Direct taxes are levied directly on the income or wealth of individuals or organizations, and the burden cannot be shifted.

○ These taxes are mostly progressive, meaning the tax rate increases with higher income.

○ Examples:

■ Income Tax: Levied on the income of individuals and businesses.

■ Corporate Tax: Applied to the profits of companies.

■ Capital Gains Tax: Tax on the sale of capital assets.

■ Securities Transaction Tax (STT): Imposed on transactions in securities markets.

■ The Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) is responsible for administering direct taxes.
questions.solution_hi:
• प्रत्यक्ष कर, जैसे आयकर, करदाता द्वारा सीधे भुगतान किए जाते हैं।

• संपत्ति कर 2015 में समाप्त होने तक एक प्रत्यक्ष कर था।

• कॉर्पोरेट कर एक प्रत्यक्ष कर है, अप्रत्यक्ष कर नहीं, क्योंकि यह सीधे कंपनियों की आय या लाभ पर लगाया जाता है।

questions.q_en:
Which of the following statements regarding GST in India is/are correct?

a) GST is a single tax applied uniformly across all states in India.

b) The GST Council is a constitutional body under Article 279A of the Constitution.

c) GST is a regressive tax, affecting low-income groups more than high-income groups.
questions.solution_en:
• GST is a unified tax, but different states may apply different SGST rates, and the tax structure may vary.

• The GST Council was established under Article 279A of the Indian Constitution to make recommendations on GST rates and structure.

• GST is generally considered a proportional tax because the rate is the same for all, regardless of income.

Further Insight:

• Goods and Services Tax (GST)

○ Passed and added in constitution after 101st Constitutional amendment Bill 2016

○ Implemented on July 1, 2017, GST is a multi-stage, destination-based tax.

○ It is aimed at eliminating the cascading effect of previous taxes.

○ GST integrates most indirect taxes into a single tax system.

○ It is divided into CGST, SGST, and IGST (for inter-state transactions).

• GST Council:

○ Decision-making body chaired by the Finance Minister of India mentioned in Article 279A.

○ It includes the Union and State Finance Ministers.

○ The Union has 1/3rd voting power while the state has 2/3rd voting power.

■ To pass any bill it must be passed by 3/4th vote

○ The council oversees changes in GST rates, exemptions, and procedural regulations

• Exemptions under GST

○ Custom duty will be still collected along with the levy of IGST on imported goods.

○ Petroleum and tobacco products are currently exempted.

○ Excise duty on liquor, stamp duty and electricity taxes are also exempted.
questions.solution_hi:
• GST एक एकीकृत कर है, परंतु विभिन्न राज्य अलग-अलग SGST दरें लागू कर सकते हैं, व कर संरचना भिन्न हो सकती है।

• GST परिषद भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 279A के तहत GST दरों व संरचना पर सिफारिशें करने हेतु स्थापित की गई।

• GST को आमतौर पर एक आनुपातिक कर माना जाता है।

questions.q_en:
Match the following direct taxes with their descriptions:

Column 1Column 2
i. Wealth Taxa. Tax on the trading of securities in stock exchanges
ii. Corporate Taxb. Tax on income from the sale of assets
iii. Capital Gains Taxc. Abolished in 2015
iv. Securities Transaction Taxd. Tax on company profits
questions.solution_en:
• Wealth Tax: Abolished in 2015.

• Corporate Tax: Tax on company profits.

• Capital Gains Tax: Tax on income from the sale of assets.

• Securities Transaction Tax: Tax on trading of securities in stock exchanges.

Further Insight:

• Direct Taxes

○ Direct taxes are levied directly on the income or wealth of individuals or organizations, and the burden cannot be shifted. These taxes are mostly progressive, meaning the tax rate increases with higher income.

○ Examples:

■ Income Tax: Levied on the income of individuals and businesses.

■ Corporate Tax: Applied to the profits of companies.

■ Capital Gains Tax: Tax on the sale of capital assets.

■ Securities Transaction Tax (STT): Imposed on transactions in securities markets.

○ The Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) is responsible for administering direct taxes.

• Indirect Taxes

○ Indirect taxes are levied on goods and services, where the tax burden is passed on to the final consumer. These are typically regressive as they apply uniformly regardless of income.

○ Examples:

■ Goods and Services Tax (GST): A comprehensive tax covering all goods and services.

■ Customs Duty: Levied on imports and exports.

■ Excise Duty: Levied on the production of goods within the country.

○ The Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC) administers indirect taxes.
questions.solution_hi:
• संपत्ति कर: 2015 में समाप्त।

• कॉर्पोरेट कर: कंपनी के लाभ पर कर।

• पूँजीगत लाभ कर: संपत्ति बिक्री से आय पर कर।

• प्रतिभूति लेनदेन कर: शेयर बाजारों में प्रतिभूतियों के व्यापार पर कर।

• प्रत्यक्ष कर: प्रत्यक्ष कर सीधे लगाए जाते हैं।

questions.q_en:
Match the following terms with their historical context:

Column 1Column 2
i. Jizyaa. Introduced by Lord Cornwallis in Bengal
ii. Permanent Settlementb. Tax system directly between the government and farmers
iii. Mahalwari Systemc. Tax on non-Muslims by Mughal rulers
iv. Ryotwari Systemd. Tax collected from village as unit
questions.solution_en:
• Jizya: Tax on non-Muslims by Mughal rulers (c).

• Permanent Settlement: Introduced by Lord Cornwallis in Bengal (a).

• In Mahalwari system tax was collected from the village as a unit.

• Ryotwari System: Tax system directly between the government and farmers (b).

Further Insight:

Permanent Settlement (1793)

○ Introduced by Lord Cornwallis

○ It was implemented in Bengal, Bihar, parts of Orissa

○ Key Provisions:

■ Revenue was a fixed annual amount, not subject to revision.

■ Zamindars (landowners) were responsible for paying the fixed revenue.

○ Led to commercialization and exploitation of farmers( zamindars had control over peasants, often leading to economic distress among farmers.)

• Ryotwari System

○ Introduced by Thomas Munro

○ Implemented in Madras, Bombay, parts of Assam, Central India

○ Key Provisions:

■ Revenue was directly assessed on the land and crop yield, with payments made by individual farmers (ryots).

■ Farmers had occupancy rights and were directly accountable to the government.

○ It provided more security to farmers and was adaptable to local conditions, though it faced challenges with land records and revenue assessment.

• Mahalwari System

• Introduced by: Holt Mackenzie

• Implemented in North-Western Provinces (now Uttar Pradesh), Punjab, Central India

• Key Provisions:

○ Revenue was collected from the head of a mahal (village or group of villages) based on land productivity.

○ Land Tenure: Shared responsibility among the community; the revenue was based on collective accountability.

• Impact: Aimed to balance interests but often led to administrative complexities and disputes over land rights.
questions.solution_hi:
• जज़िया: मुगल शासकों द्वारा गैर-मुसलमानों पर कर (c)।

• स्थायी बंदोबस्त: बंगाल में लॉर्ड कॉर्नवालिस द्वारा पेश किया गया (a)।

• महालवारी प्रणाली में गाँव को एक इकाई के रूप में कर एकत्रित किया जाता था।

• रैयतवारी प्रणाली: सरकार व किसानों के बीच सीधा कर प्रणाली (b)।

questions.q_en:
Match the following state taxes with their correct descriptions:

Column 1Column 2
i. Stamp Dutya. Tax on fuel and alcohol
ii. Entertainment Taxb. Levied on property transactions and legal documents
iii. VATc. Imposed on movie tickets and entertainment events
iv. State Excise Dutyd. Still applicable on some goods despite GST
questions.solution_en:
• Stamp Duty: Levied on property transactions and legal documents (b).

• Entertainment Tax: Imposed on movie tickets and entertainment events (c).

• VAT: Still applicable on certain items like fuel, even after GST (d).

• State Excise Duty: Applied to alcohol and narcotics (a).

Further Insight:

• Central Taxes:

○ Taxes levied and collected by the Central Government:

■ Income Tax: Tax on individual income.

■ Excise Duty: On production and manufacturing of goods.

■ Customs Duty: Tax on imports and exports.

■ CGST (Central Goods and Services Tax): Component of GST on intra-state transactions.

• State Taxes:

○ Levied by State Governments:

■ State Goods and Services Tax (SGST): State portion of GST for intra-state sales.

■ Stamp Duty: On property transactions and official documents.

■ Entertainment Tax: On events like movies and concerts (now mostly subsumed under GST).
questions.solution_hi:
• स्टाम्प शुल्क: संपत्ति लेनदेन व कानूनी दस्तावेजों पर लगाया जाता है (b)।

• मनोरंजन कर: फिल्म टिकट व मनोरंजन आयोजनों पर लगाया जाता है (c)।

• VAT: GST के बाद भी ईंधन जैसी कुछ वस्तुओं पर अभी भी लागू (d)।

• राज्य उत्पाद शुल्क: शराब व नशीले पदार्थों पर लागू (a)।
